purpose: Human-reviewable plan consumed by Scripts/release_aron_alignment.py: rigid XY translation of the TEMPLE actor set (route A) so that the Aron footprint centre sits over the Dome of the Rock centroid (Even HaShetiyah / es-Sakhra) within the stated uncertainty. Numbers come from SourceAssets/scale-review/aron-alignment-plan-*.json written by Scripts/plan_aron_alignment.py. Nothing here claims the rock's centre is known better than about 4 m, and nothing here changes the vertical datum.

Main50.reason: The Aron centre (-6200, 0) is 100 cm from the Dome centroid (-6300, 0); the rock centre is uncertain by about 424 cm. Applying requires -AronAlignAllowNotRecommended in addition to -AronAlignApply.

Candidate48.lastKnownMapSha256Provenance: Observed by dry run aron-alignment-release-Candidate48-20260908T214539156783Z.json and on disk 2026-09-08 21:5x UTC, after the candidate-spawn-fix receipts of 19:21-19:23 UTC changed the map. Previous handoff value 8dc55f79b3dbcfe0ba7a15c41b3fb2da5be108766aab5a2cf7a9aae46f8a8f89. Apply refuses if the map changes again.
Candidate48.reason: Re-pivot: the .96 conversion was pivoted at the outer altar (origin), sliding the Aron 248 cm east to -5952. Translating the converted Temple by -248 and moving the Selected48 descriptor pivot to the legacy Aron (-6200, 0, 0) is the same as having scaled about the Aron; the runtime adapters follow the descriptor. Residual to the Dome centroid: 100 cm, same as main; not chased.

descriptor.consistencyRule: Scaling a legacy point P about pivot Q by r gives Q + (P - Q) r = r P + Q (1 - r): the same as scaling about the origin and translating by Q (1 - r). With r = .96 and Q = (-6200, 0, 0) the translation is (-248, 0, 0) = deltaCm; equivalently after = deltaCm / (1 - r).

lastKnownMapSha256History.reason: release_enclosure.py -EnclosureTarget=Candidate48 saved the candidate (receipt native-enclosure-Candidate48-20260908T215500489017Z.json); reviewed by the coordinator, not a blind bump

classification.note: Every level actor must fall into exactly one bucket or the run refuses (dry run: reports). Temple actors move; context, globals and frame-adapted actors do not.

enginePrimitiveRule.rule: An engine primitive is used by both sides (tour markers = Cylinder, Kotel photo panels = Plane). It counts as a context mesh only when NO templeLabelPrefixes entry matches the label; a Temple label prefix on a primitive classifies as Temple. A primitive alone (no label match) never classifies as Temple. Proven by classifier_self_test() in the script, run offline and before every live classification.
enginePrimitiveRule.originatingDryRun: aron-alignment-release-Candidate48-20260908T214539156783Z.json: 18 RELEASE_TOUR_Marker_* actors AMBIGUOUS (the log shows 36 lines because UE echoes each LogPython warning twice; one marker actor per stop).

tourMarkers.rule: ALL 18 RELEASE_TOUR_Marker_<nn>_<key> StaticMeshActors move with the Temple (temple_respawn), including the three deck stops mount-and-house (legacy X 12000), immersion (11000) and soreg-and-cheil (10000).
tourMarkers.why: AMikdashTourGuide converts EVERY stop's stand/look through MikdashSceneUnits::TryLegacyTemplePoint(TourFrame, ...) (MikdashTourGuide.cpp lines 374 and 548); there is no per-stop frame flag in tour-stops.json. Scripts/release_amah48_tour.py placed the candidate markers at stand x .96 for all 18 stops (12000 -> 11520, 11000 -> 10560, 10000 -> 9600). Marker and runtime stand therefore share one frame; when the descriptor pivot moves to (-6200,0,0) the runtime stands shift by -248 cm and the markers must shift identically or the discs no longer sit under the arrival radius.
tourMarkers.finding: The deck stops were scaled about the origin as if they were Temple frame. On the flat Z 0 Mount deck (X to +149 m) that is a harmless 4.4-4.8 m westward slide (soreg-and-cheil is genuinely Temple architecture, the outer envelope reaching X 92 m), but mount-and-house and immersion are conceptually metric context. Making them metric needs a per-stop frame flag in tour-stops.json and TourGuide/TourMath - a tour-placement rule outside this script's ownership, not something a translation should paper over.

frameAdaptedClasses.note: Actors whose Temple coordinates live in properties (polygons, station points, control points) and are converted at run time through the Selected48 descriptor. They are NOT moved by this script; the descriptor pivot change carries them on Candidate48. On Main50 they would need their properties/specs rewritten (see hardcoded list in the plan receipt) - another reason Main50 is not recommended.

moveMethod.other: actor.modify(True); root_component.modify(True); set_actor_location(new, sweep=False, teleport=True) - the pattern release_amah48_frame.py used for PlayerStart_0 and verified after reopen
moveMethod.why: static-mobility StaticMeshActors do not reliably dirty their package on a transform change; a re-spawned actor is a new export and always saves

limitations: The rock centre is modelled as the OSM Dome of the Rock polygon centroid with a 424 cm uncertainty radius; no plan giving the Sakhra's offset inside the dome could be verified offline.
XY only. The Aron floor stays about 13.2-13.6 m above the published 743.7 m rock summit; the vertical datum is a separate decision.

Component-level material overrides on re-spawned actors are copied per slot; any other per-component customisation not listed in moveMethod.respawnCopies is NOT copied and the pre-move snapshot in the receipt is the evidence for restoring it.
Runtime acceptance (PIE walking, tour route legality, crowd zones, service stations, save/load identity) is not established by this script; it verifies numeric placement only.
